name: Lim dynasty of Mari
alt: Second kingdom of Mari under the Lim dynasty

successors.name: Babylonia
successors.text: the Suhum region, which "became a Babylonian province" after 1761

ledger.x: c. 1830 BC: Mari becomes the seat of the Lim dynasty. "Mari became the seat of the Amorite Lim dynasty under king Yaggid-Lim" c. 1830 BC; the page notes it is not certain he controlled Mari, and that "in c. 1820 BC Yahdun-Lim was firmly in control as king of Mari". The land is Mari's district.

c. 1810 BC (bridged to mid-reign): Yahdun-Lim holds Tuttul and expands up the Euphrates. His titles were "king of Mari, Tuttul, and the land of Hana"; "He defeated the Yaminite rebels centered at Tuttul"; the pages give no year (reign c. 1820-1797) and the Mediterranean campaign he "claimed" is undated and…

c. 1796 BC: Shamshi-Adad I takes Mari. Yahdun-Lim "was assassinated in c. 1798 BC by his possible son Sumu-Yamam" (also: killed in battle with Shamshi-Adad c. 1796); Sumu-Yamam "was assassinated two years after taking the throne, and Shamshi-Adad then annexed Mari", appointing Yasmah-Adad; the rest of the Lim family…

c. 1776 BC: Zimri-Lim returns to Mari. The Mari page: "a short time after his enthronement in c. 1776 BC"; Zimri-Lim's page: Samsi-Addu died in 1775, Yasmah-Addu disappeared from the record and Zimri-Lim "entered Mari and was crowned in Terqa". Shamshi-Adad I's page: "Yasmah-Adad was soon expelled from Mari by…

c. 1775 BC: Zimri-Lim takes Tuttul and Terqa. "Zimri-Lim advanced along the Euphrates, taking Tuttul and then Terqa." The page adds that Bannum, a Bensimalite warlord, seized Mari, and that Ishme-Dagan "kept Ekallatum but could not intervene in Mari".
ledger.cp: Yaminite and Bensimalite chiefs (Tuttul, Terqa, Mari)

ledger.x: c. 1775 BC (bridged): the Suhum region. The pages say nothing of how Mari got Suhum; the Zimri-Lim page has Eshnunna invading it in fall 1772, and the Mari page has it a Babylonian province after 1761. Held by 1772, so shown from the restoration. Page silent on the date and the previous holder.

c. 1771 BC: the Upper Khabur. Zimri-Lim "defeated Qarni-Lim of Andarig, securing the Mariote control over the region in c. 1771 BC", and "expanded into the Upper Khabur region (Idamaraz)". The Zimri-Lim page has Eshnunna defeated at Andarig (no year).

c. 1761 BC: Hammurabi ends the Lim dynasty. "Babylon invaded in c. 1761 BC under the rule of Hammurabi and defeated Zimri-Lin, ending the Lim dynasty." Terqa became the capital of the rump Kingdom of Hana and the Suhum region a Babylonian province; the Zimri-Lim page: Babylon captured Mari "apparently in the spring of…

wars.name: Yahdun-Lim against the Yaminites and Shamshi-Adad I
wars.outcome: Yahdun-Lim defeated the Yaminite rebels at Tuttul (backed by Sumu-Epuh of Yamhad) and avoided open war with Yamhad; "later lost a war to Shamshi-Adad" and died c.

wars.name: Shamshi-Adad I's annexation of Mari
wars.outcome: Shamshi-Adad I put Yasmah-Adad on the throne of Mari c.

wars.name: Zimri-Lim's restoration along the Euphrates
wars.outcome: Zimri-Lim took Tuttul and then Terqa and entered Mari; Bannum, a Bensimalite warlord, held Mari for a time.

wars.name: Mari-Eshnunna war
wars.outcome: Eshnunna invaded Suhum in fall 1772; its forces were defeated at Andarig; peace in 1770 with the lost territories regained.

wars.name: Elamite war and the coalition with Babylon
wars.outcome: Mari allied with Elam in 1766-1765; Elam "captured it [Eshnunna] in 1765"; Zimri-Lim and Hammurabi then defeated the Elamites at Hiritum in northern Babylonia (undated).

certainty.note: The pages give titles and provincial seats, not a frontier.
The Lim dynasty held no land: Mari was Shamshi-Adad I's (assyria dossier) and the family was in exile.
The Upper Khabur and Suhum limits are readings; Andarig is unlocated on the pages.
